claim: Most nervous systems combine both transmitter-mediated and direct cell–cell communication, known as 'chemical' and 'electrical' synapses, respectively.
source: Most nervous systems combine both transmitter-mediated and direct cell–cell communication, known as 'chemical' and 'electrical' synapses, respectively.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about nervous system organization.

claim: Chemical synapses can be identified by their multiple structural components.
source: Chemical synapses can be identified by their multiple structural components.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about chemical synapse structure.

claim: Electrical synapses are generally defined by the presence of a 'gap junction' (a cluster of intercellular channels) between two neuronal processes.
source: Electrical synapses are, on the other hand, generally defined by the presence of a 'gap junction' (a cluster of intercellular channels) between two neuronal processes.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about electrical synapse structure.

claim: Gap junctions provide the communicating mechanism for electrical transmission.
source: However, while gap junctions provide the communicating mechanism, it is unknown whether electrical transmission requires the contribution of additional cellular structures.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about gap junction function.

claim: It is unknown whether electrical transmission requires the contribution of additional cellular structures beyond gap junctions.
source: However, while gap junctions provide the communicating mechanism, it is unknown whether electrical transmission requires the contribution of additional cellular structures.
evidence: This represents a gap in current scientific knowledge that the study aims to address.

claim: At zebrafish Mauthner cell synaptic contacts, gap junctions coexist with specializations for neurotransmitter release.
source: We investigated this question at identifiable single synaptic contacts on the zebrafish Mauthner cells, at which gap junctions coexist with specializations for neurotransmitter release and where the contact unequivocally defines the anatomical limits of a synapse.
evidence: This is supported by prior knowledge and observations at these specific synapses.

claim: The synaptic contact at zebrafish Mauthner cells unequivocally defines the anatomical limits of a synapse.
source: We investigated this question at identifiable single synaptic contacts on the zebrafish Mauthner cells, at which gap junctions coexist with specializations for neurotransmitter release and where the contact unequivocally defines the anatomical limits of a synapse.
evidence: This is based on the known anatomical structure of these synapses.

claim: Expansion microscopy of single Mauthner cell contacts revealed a detailed map of the incidence and spatial distribution of proteins pertaining to various synaptic structures.
source: Expansion microscopy of these single contacts revealed a detailed map of the incidence and spatial distribution of proteins pertaining to various synaptic structures.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Multiple gap junctions of variable size were identified by the presence of their molecular components at Mauthner cell contacts.
source: Multiple gap junctions of variable size were identified by the presence of their molecular components.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from expansion microscopy and immunolabeling.

claim: Most of the synaptic contact's surface was occupied by interleaving gap junctions and components of adherens junctions.
source: Remarkably, most of the synaptic contact's surface was occupied by interleaving gap junctions and components of adherens junctions, suggesting a close functional association between these two structures.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on expansion microscopy data and quantitative analysis.

claim: The interleaving distribution of gap junctions and adherens junctions suggests a close functional association between these two structures.
source: Remarkably, most of the synaptic contact's surface was occupied by interleaving gap junctions and components of adherens junctions, suggesting a close functional association between these two structures.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observed spatial distribution of these structures.

claim: Glutamate receptors were confined to small peripheral portions of the contact at Mauthner cell synapses.
source: In contrast, glutamate receptors were confined to small peripheral portions of the contact, indicating that most of the synaptic area functions as an electrical synapse.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunolabeling and expansion microscopy.

claim: Most of the synaptic area at Mauthner cell contacts functions as an electrical synapse.
source: In contrast, glutamate receptors were confined to small peripheral portions of the contact, indicating that most of the synaptic area functions as an electrical synapse.
evidence: This is inferred from the spatial distribution of gap junction proteins versus glutamate receptors.

claim: An electrical synapse operates with not one, but multiple gap junctions.
source: Thus, our results revealed the overarching organization of an electrical synapse that operates with not one, but multiple gap junctions, in close association with structural and signaling molecules known to be components of adherens junctions.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion based on the experimental data showing multiple gap junction puncta.

claim: Electrical synapses operate in close association with structural and signaling molecules known to be components of adherens junctions.
source: Thus, our results revealed the overarching organization of an electrical synapse that operates with not one, but multiple gap junctions, in close association with structural and signaling molecules known to be components of adherens junctions.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing colocalization and spatial distribution of these components.

claim: The relationship between gap junctions and adherens junctions will aid in establishing the boundaries of electrical synapses found throughout animal connectomes.
source: The relationship between these intercellular structures will aid in establishing the boundaries of electrical synapses found throughout animal connectomes and provide insight into the structural organization and functional diversity of electrical synapses.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential applications of the findings.

claim: Understanding the relationship between gap junctions and adherens junctions will provide insight into the structural organization and functional diversity of electrical synapses.
source: The relationship between these intercellular structures will aid in establishing the boundaries of electrical synapses found throughout animal connectomes and provide insight into the structural organization and functional diversity of electrical synapses.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the implications of the findings.

claim: Synapses are specialized cell–cell contacts where two neurons can share relevant functional information.
source: Synapses are specialized cell–cell contacts where two neurons can share relevant functional information.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about synapse function.

claim: The exchange of information at synapses can occur directly through cell–cell channels, known as 'electrical synapses', or indirectly, via the release of a chemical messenger, known as 'chemical synapses'.
source: The exchange of information can occur directly through cell–cell channels, known as 'electrical synapses', or indirectly, via the release of a chemical messenger, known as 'chemical synapses' (Pereda, 2014).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The molecular complexity of chemical synapses with structurally distinct pre- and postsynaptic components has long been recognized.
source: While the molecular complexity of chemical synapses with structurally distinct pre- and postsynaptic components has long been recognized (Wichmann and Kuner, 2022; Wilhelm et al., 2014), less is known regarding the molecular and structural complexity of electrical synapses.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Less is known regarding the molecular and structural complexity of electrical synapses compared to chemical synapses.
source: While the molecular complexity of chemical synapses with structurally distinct pre- and postsynaptic components has long been recognized (Wichmann and Kuner, 2022; Wilhelm et al., 2014), less is known regarding the molecular and structural complexity of electrical synapses.
evidence: This represents a gap in current scientific knowledge.

claim: Gap junctions contain intercellular channels formed by the apposition of two hemichannels, each provided by one of the connected cells.
source: These structures contain intercellular channels formed by the apposition of two hemichannels, each provided by one of the connected cells, and which cluster together into GJ 'plaques' (Goodenough and Paul, 2009).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Gap junction channels cluster together into GJ 'plaques'.
source: These structures contain intercellular channels formed by the apposition of two hemichannels, each provided by one of the connected cells, and which cluster together into GJ 'plaques' (Goodenough and Paul, 2009).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Hemichannels are formed by proteins called 'connexins' in vertebrates.
source: Hemichannels are formed by proteins called 'connexins' (Goodenough and Paul, 2009; Söhl and Willecke, 2004) in vertebrates and 'innexins' (Phelan et al., 1998; Phelan, 2005) in invertebrates that, though unrelated in sequence, share a similar membrane topology that allows them to assemble into intercellular channels.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Hemichannels are formed by proteins called 'innexins' in invertebrates.
source: Hemichannels are formed by proteins called 'connexins' (Goodenough and Paul, 2009; Söhl and Willecke, 2004) in vertebrates and 'innexins' (Phelan et al., 1998; Phelan, 2005) in invertebrates that, though unrelated in sequence, share a similar membrane topology that allows them to assemble into intercellular channels.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Connexins and innexins, though unrelated in sequence, share a similar membrane topology that allows them to assemble into intercellular channels.
source: Hemichannels are formed by proteins called 'connexins' (Goodenough and Paul, 2009; Söhl and Willecke, 2004) in vertebrates and 'innexins' (Phelan et al., 1998; Phelan, 2005) in invertebrates that, though unrelated in sequence, share a similar membrane topology that allows them to assemble into intercellular channels.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Gap junctions are ubiquitous and present in virtually every tissue of the organism providing metabolic coupling.
source: While GJs are ubiquitous and present in virtually every tissue of the organism providing metabolic coupling (Goodenough and Paul, 2009), they additionally serve as a pathway of low resistance for the spread of electrical currents between neurons (and cells of the heart), the main form of signaling in the brain, which is fast enough to operate within the time frame required for decision-making by neural circuits (Bennett, 1997; Alcamí and Pereda, 2019).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Gap junctions serve as a pathway of low resistance for the spread of electrical currents between neurons and cells of the heart.
source: While GJs are ubiquitous and present in virtually every tissue of the organism providing metabolic coupling (Goodenough and Paul, 2009), they additionally serve as a pathway of low resistance for the spread of electrical currents between neurons (and cells of the heart), the main form of signaling in the brain, which is fast enough to operate within the time frame required for decision-making by neural circuits (Bennett, 1997; Alcamí and Pereda, 2019).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Electrical signaling through gap junctions is fast enough to operate within the time frame required for decision-making by neural circuits.
source: While GJs are ubiquitous and present in virtually every tissue of the organism providing metabolic coupling (Goodenough and Paul, 2009), they additionally serve as a pathway of low resistance for the spread of electrical currents between neurons (and cells of the heart), the main form of signaling in the brain, which is fast enough to operate within the time frame required for decision-making by neural circuits (Bennett, 1997; Alcamí and Pereda, 2019).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Electrical synapses are generally perceived as structurally simpler than chemical synapses and exclusively involving the function of intercellular channels.
source: Electrical synapses are generally perceived as structurally simpler than chemical synapses and exclusively involving the function of intercellular channels.
evidence: This represents a common perception in the field that the authors are challenging.

claim: Recent data indicates that the function of gap junction channels is under the control of their supporting molecular scaffold.
source: However, recent data indicates that the function of these channels is under the control of their supporting molecular scaffold (Flores et al., 2008; Lasseigne et al., 2021; Martin et al., 2020; Martin et al., 2023), suggesting that neuronal GJs are complex molecular structures whose function requires the contribution of multiple molecular components (Miller and Pereda, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent research.

claim: Neuronal gap junctions are complex molecular structures whose function requires the contribution of multiple molecular components.
source: However, recent data indicates that the function of these channels is under the control of their supporting molecular scaffold (Flores et al., 2008; Lasseigne et al., 2021; Martin et al., 2020; Martin et al., 2023), suggesting that neuronal GJs are complex molecular structures whose function requires the contribution of multiple molecular components (Miller and Pereda, 2017).
evidence: This is an inference supported by citations to recent research.

claim: Molecular complexity of gap junctions is likely to underlie plastic changes in the strength of electrical synapses.
source: Such molecular complexity is likely to underlie plastic changes in the strength of electrical synapses (Pereda et al., 2013; O'Brien and Bloomfield, 2018), which are capable of dynamically reconfiguring neural circuits (O'Brien and Bloomfield, 2018; Bloomfield and Völgyi, 2009).
evidence: This is an inference supported by citations to research on synaptic plasticity.

claim: Electrical synapses are capable of dynamically reconfiguring neural circuits.
source: Such molecular complexity is likely to underlie plastic changes in the strength of electrical synapses (Pereda et al., 2013; O'Brien and Bloomfield, 2018), which are capable of dynamically reconfiguring neural circuits (O'Brien and Bloomfield, 2018; Bloomfield and Völgyi, 2009).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Investigations of vertebrate electrical transmission have solely considered the functional properties of connexins, the molecules that regulate them, and their interactions at the GJ plaque.
source: Thus far, investigations of the properties of vertebrate electrical transmission have solely considered the functional properties of the channel-forming proteins, the connexins, the molecules that regulate them, and their interactions at the GJ plaque.
evidence: This describes the current state of research in the field.

claim: The identification of the structural components of a chemical synapse is facilitated by the presynaptic bouton, which anatomically defines its limit.
source: The identification of the structural components of a chemical synapse is facilitated by the presynaptic bouton, which anatomically defines its limit (Sotelo, 2020).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Neuronal gap junctions are typically found connecting cell somata or other neuronal processes such as dendrites and axons.
source: In contrast, neuronal GJs are typically found connecting cell somata or other neuronal processes (Alcamí and Pereda, 2019; Sotelo, 2020; Sotelo and Llinás, 1972), such as dendrites and axons, making it more difficult to define the exact anatomical boundaries that constitute an electrical synapse.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The typical location of neuronal gap junctions makes it more difficult to define the exact anatomical boundaries that constitute an electrical synapse.
source: In contrast, neuronal GJs are typically found connecting cell somata or other neuronal processes (Alcamí and Pereda, 2019; Sotelo, 2020; Sotelo and Llinás, 1972), such as dendrites and axons, making it more difficult to define the exact anatomical boundaries that constitute an electrical synapse.
evidence: This is an inference based on the anatomical characteristics of gap junctions.

claim: Neuronal gap junctions can occur at synaptic boutons, generally coexisting with specializations for chemical transmission.
source: Neuronal GJs can also occur at synaptic boutons, generally coexisting with specializations for chemical transmission (Sotelo, 2020; Martin and Pilar, 1963).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Auditory afferents terminate as single 'large myelinated club endings' or 'club endings' on the lateral dendrite of teleost Mauthner cells.
source: This is the case for auditory afferents terminating as single 'large myelinated club endings' (Bartelmez, 1915; Bartelmez and Hoerr, 1933) or 'club endings' (CEs) on the lateral dendrite of the teleost Mauthner cells (a pair of large reticulospinal neurons involved in tail-flip escape responses in fish) (Pereda and Faber, 2011; Faber and Pereda, 2011), each containing GJs and specializations for chemical transmission (Robertson et al., 1963).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Mauthner cells are a pair of large reticulospinal neurons involved in tail-flip escape responses in fish.
source: This is the case for auditory afferents terminating as single 'large myelinated club endings' (Bartelmez, 1915; Bartelmez and Hoerr, 1933) or 'club endings' (CEs) on the lateral dendrite of the teleost Mauthner cells (a pair of large reticulospinal neurons involved in tail-flip escape responses in fish) (Pereda and Faber, 2011; Faber and Pereda, 2011), each containing GJs and specializations for chemical transmission (Robertson et al., 1963).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Club endings contain gap junctions and specializations for chemical transmission.
source: This is the case for auditory afferents terminating as single 'large myelinated club endings' (Bartelmez, 1915; Bartelmez and Hoerr, 1933) or 'club endings' (CEs) on the lateral dendrite of the teleost Mauthner cells (a pair of large reticulospinal neurons involved in tail-flip escape responses in fish) (Pereda and Faber, 2011; Faber and Pereda, 2011), each containing GJs and specializations for chemical transmission (Robertson et al., 1963).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Club endings are considered a valuable model to study vertebrate electrical transmission because of their experimental accessibility and functional properties.
source: Because of their experimental accessibly and functional properties, these terminals are considered a valuable model to study vertebrate electrical transmission as they more easily allow for the correlation between structure and function of synaptic features (Pereda et al., 2013; Robertson et al., 1963; Furshpan, 1964; Flores et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Club endings allow for easier correlation between structure and function of synaptic features.
source: Because of their experimental accessibly and functional properties, these terminals are considered a valuable model to study vertebrate electrical transmission as they more easily allow for the correlation between structure and function of synaptic features (Pereda et al., 2013; Robertson et al., 1963; Furshpan, 1964; Flores et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The presynaptic bouton marks the anatomical limits of a synapse at club endings.
source: Since the bouton marks the anatomical limits of a synapse, these contacts offer the opportunity to examine the anatomical structures that together make an electrical synapse.
evidence: This is based on the known anatomical structure of these synapses.

claim: Club endings offer the opportunity to examine the anatomical structures that together make an electrical synapse.
source: Since the bouton marks the anatomical limits of a synapse, these contacts offer the opportunity to examine the anatomical structures that together make an electrical synapse.
evidence: This is an inference based on the anatomical characteristics of club endings.

claim: Club endings from larval zebrafish share comparable morphological and functional properties with those of adult fish.
source: CEs from larval zebrafish share comparable morphological and functional properties with those of adult fish (Lasseigne et al., 2021; Yao et al., 2014; Miller et al., 2017; Echeverry et al., 2022), and due to their genetic accessibility, allow for the opportunity to investigate the functional link between the structures enabling electrical transmission and its regulation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to research comparing larval and adult fish.

claim: Larval zebrafish club endings allow for the opportunity to investigate the functional link between the structures enabling electrical transmission and its regulation due to their genetic accessibility.
source: CEs from larval zebrafish share comparable morphological and functional properties with those of adult fish (Lasseigne et al., 2021; Yao et al., 2014; Miller et al., 2017; Echeverry et al., 2022), and due to their genetic accessibility, allow for the opportunity to investigate the functional link between the structures enabling electrical transmission and its regulation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the genetic tractability of zebrafish.

claim: Expansion revealed the presence of multiple well-defined puncta distributed throughout the contact area at club endings.
source: Expansion revealed the presence of multiple well-defined puncta distributed throughout the contact area, which, consistent with the notion that they represent GJ plaques, each exhibited labeling for the fish homologs of the widespread mammalian connexin 36 (Cx36), Cx35, and Cx34, as well as for the GJ scaffolding protein zonula occludens (ZO1) (Flores et al., 2008; Lasseigne et al., 2021; Miller et al., 2017; Rash et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on expansion microscopy data.

claim: The puncta observed at club endings represent gap junction plaques.
source: Expansion revealed the presence of multiple well-defined puncta distributed throughout the contact area, which, consistent with the notion that they represent GJ plaques, each exhibited labeling for the fish homologs of the widespread mammalian connexin 36 (Cx36), Cx35, and Cx34, as well as for the GJ scaffolding protein zonula occludens (ZO1) (Flores et al., 2008; Lasseigne et al., 2021; Miller et al., 2017; Rash et al., 2013).
evidence: This is inferred from the labeling of gap junction proteins at these puncta.

claim: Each punctum at club endings exhibited labeling for Cx35 and Cx34, fish homologs of mammalian connexin 36.
source: Expansion revealed the presence of multiple well-defined puncta distributed throughout the contact area, which, consistent with the notion that they represent GJ plaques, each exhibited labeling for the fish homologs of the widespread mammalian connexin 36 (Cx36), Cx35, and Cx34, as well as for the GJ scaffolding protein zonula occludens (ZO1) (Flores et al., 2008; Lasseigne et al., 2021; Miller et al., 2017; Rash et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunolabeling and expansion microscopy.

claim: Each punctum at club endings exhibited labeling for the gap junction scaffolding protein zonula occludens (ZO1).
source: Expansion revealed the presence of multiple well-defined puncta distributed throughout the contact area, which, consistent with the notion that they represent GJ plaques, each exhibited labeling for the fish homologs of the widespread mammalian connexin 36 (Cx36), Cx35, and Cx34, as well as for the GJ scaffolding protein zonula occludens (ZO1) (Flores et al., 2008; Lasseigne et al., 2021; Miller et al., 2017; Rash et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunolabeling and expansion microscopy.

claim: Expansion following staining with N-cadherin and ß-catenin antibodies showed that these proteins are distributed throughout the contact area in a fashion that is mutually exclusive with connexin.
source: Strikingly, expansion following staining with N-cadherin and ß-catenin antibodies, protein components of 'adherens junctions' (AJs), showed that these proteins are also distributed all throughout the contact area, but in a fashion that is mutually exclusive with connexin.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on expansion microscopy and immunolabeling data.

claim: The mutually exclusive distribution of adherens junction proteins and connexin suggests that the subsynaptic topography of electrical synapses is carefully and intimately coordinated.
source: This suggests that the subsynaptic topography of electrical synapses is carefully and intimately coordinated.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observed spatial distribution patterns.

claim: Double labeling with Cx and glutamate receptor antibodies showed that gap junctions are distributed throughout the entire contact area.
source: Finally, double labeling with Cx and glutamate receptor antibodies showed that, while GJs are distributed throughout the entire contact area, a much smaller number of glutamatergic sites are restricted to the periphery occupying a small fraction (~19%) of the contact's surface.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunolabeling and expansion microscopy.

claim: A much smaller number of glutamatergic sites are restricted to the periphery occupying approximately 19% of the contact's surface at club endings.
source: Finally, double labeling with Cx and glutamate receptor antibodies showed that, while GJs are distributed throughout the entire contact area, a much smaller number of glutamatergic sites are restricted to the periphery occupying a small fraction (~19%) of the contact's surface.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunolabeling, expansion microscopy, and quantitative analysis.

claim: Synaptic communication at electrical synapses results from the coordinated action of multiple gap junctions of variable size.
source: Thus, our data suggest that synaptic communication at electrical synapses results from not one but the coordinated action of multiple GJs of variable size, which may require the functional contribution of additional structures, such as AJs.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the experimental data showing multiple gap junctions.

claim: Electrical synapses may require the functional contribution of additional structures, such as adherens junctions.
source: Thus, our data suggest that synaptic communication at electrical synapses results from not one but the coordinated action of multiple GJs of variable size, which may require the functional contribution of additional structures, such as AJs.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the observed close association between gap junctions and adherens junctions.

claim: Ultrastructural analysis of club endings in adult goldfish revealed the presence of gap junctions coexisting with specializations for neurotransmitter release.
source: Ultrastructural analysis of CEs in adult goldfish (Robertson et al., 1963; Tuttle et al., 1986; Kohno and Noguchi, 1986) and larval zebrafish (Yao et al., 2014) revealed the presence of GJs coexisting with specializations for neurotransmitter release.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Ultrastructural analysis of club endings in larval zebrafish revealed the presence of gap junctions coexisting with specializations for neurotransmitter release.
source: Ultrastructural analysis of CEs in adult goldfish (Robertson et al., 1963; Tuttle et al., 1986; Kohno and Noguchi, 1986) and larval zebrafish (Yao et al., 2014) revealed the presence of GJs coexisting with specializations for neurotransmitter release.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Stimulation of club endings evokes a synaptic response that combines electrical and chemical transmission.
source: Consistent with these synaptic specializations, stimulation of CEs evokes a synaptic response that combines electrical and chemical transmission (Furshpan, 1964; Yao et al., 2014; Echeverry et al., 2022; Lin and Faber, 1988).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Gap junctions at club endings consist of heterotypic intercellular channels created by the apposition of a presynaptic hemichannel formed by connexin Cx35.5 and a postsynaptic hemichannel formed by Cx34.1.
source: A wealth of evidence indicates that GJs at these terminals consist of heterotypic intercellular channels created by the apposition of a presynaptic hemichannel formed by connexin Cx35.5 and a postsynaptic hemichannel formed by Cx34.1, two of the Cx35 (Cx35.1 and Cx35.5) and Cx34 (Cx34.1 and Cx34.7) orthologs (Miller et al., 2017; Rash et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Gap junctions at club endings contain the scaffolding protein ZO1.
source: These junctions also contain the scaffolding protein ZO1 (Flores et al., 2008; Lasseigne et al., 2021), which regulates channel function.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: ZO1 regulates gap junction channel function at club endings.
source: These junctions also contain the scaffolding protein ZO1 (Flores et al., 2008; Lasseigne et al., 2021), which regulates channel function.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The synaptic contact areas of club endings can be visualized and unambiguously identified by immunolabeling for gap junction proteins.
source: The synaptic contact areas of CEs (Figure 1A) can be visualized and unambiguously identified by immunolabeling for these GJ proteins, which are revealed as large fluorescent oval areas at the distal portion of the lateral dendrite of the M-cell (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunolabeling.

claim: Gap junction proteins at club endings are revealed as large fluorescent oval areas at the distal portion of the lateral dendrite of the M-cell.
source: The synaptic contact areas of CEs (Figure 1A) can be visualized and unambiguously identified by immunolabeling for these GJ proteins, which are revealed as large fluorescent oval areas at the distal portion of the lateral dendrite of the M-cell (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunolabeling shown in figures.

claim: Tissue expansion with anti-Cx35.5 revealed the presence of multiple Cx35.5-positive puncta at club ending contacts forming a concave oval area.
source: Tissue expansion with anti-Cx35.5 revealed the presence of multiple Cx35.5-positive puncta at these contacts forming a concave oval area (Figure 1E, Figure 1—video 1), reminiscent of that observed at goldfish CEs, known to correspond to GJ plaques (Flores et al., 2008; Pereda et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on expansion microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: The concave oval area formed by Cx35.5-positive puncta is reminiscent of that observed at goldfish club endings, known to correspond to gap junction plaques.
source: Tissue expansion with anti-Cx35.5 revealed the presence of multiple Cx35.5-positive puncta at these contacts forming a concave oval area (Figure 1E, Figure 1—video 1), reminiscent of that observed at goldfish CEs, known to correspond to GJ plaques (Flores et al., 2008; Pereda et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with previous observations supported by citations.

claim: The main diameter of the oval synaptic contact area increased about fourfold (3.9× expansion factor) after expansion.
source: The main diameter of the oval synaptic contact area defined by labeling of Cx35.5, either using anti-Cx35/36 (which recognizes both Cx35.5 and Cx35.1) or a specific anti-Cx35.5, or of ZO1 with anti-ZO1, increased about fourfold (3.9× expansion factor), from 2.11 ± 0.037 µm in non-expansion experiments (n = 38 CEs from 26 fish) to 8.25 ± 0.225 µm in expansion experiments (n = 40 CEs from 13 fish) (mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative measurements from expansion microscopy experiments.

claim: Expansion led to an about 13-fold increase in the area of the club ending contact.
source: Moreover, expansion led to an about 13-fold increase in the area of the contact (13.4×), from 2.63 ± 0.055 µm2 (n = 38 CEs from 26 fish) to 35.13 ± 1.266 µm2 (n = 40 CEs from 13 fish).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative measurements from expansion microscopy experiments.

claim: The average short/long diameter ratio decreased in expanded tissue compared to non-expanded tissue, with the decrease reaching statistical significance.
source: Analysis showed that the average S/L ratio decreased in the expanded tissue, with the decrease reaching statistical significance (non-expanded, 0.77 ± 0.018 [n = 38 CEs from 26 fish]; expanded, 0.64 ± 0.019 [n = 40 CEs from 13 fish]; p<0.01).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of morphometric measurements.

claim: The decrease in the average short/long diameter ratio was less than 18%.
source: However, the decrease in the average S/L ratio was less than 18%.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of the morphometric data.

claim: The distribution of short/long diameter ratios from expanded tissue was nearly identical to the distribution from non-expanded tissue.
source: Moreover, the distribution of S/L ratios from expanded tissue was nearly identical to the distribution from non-expanded tissue, and both were well described by normal distributions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The expansion procedure had no selective effects on club endings, but rather affected all uniformly.
source: This result indicates that the expansion procedure had no selective effects on CEs, but rather affected all uniformly.
evidence: This is inferred from the analysis of the distribution of short/long diameter ratios.

claim: The expansion procedure had minimal effects on synaptic structure.
source: Thus, expansion of these single synapses resulted in a more than tenfold increase of the synaptic contact area, allowing for a more detailed visualization of the relative distribution of its synaptic components.
evidence: This is inferred from the morphometric analysis and synaptic alignment findings.

claim: Colocalization analysis revealed that labeling for Cx35.5 and GluR2 was mutually exclusive.
source: As expected, colocalization analysis (Manders' coefficient analysis) revealed that labeling for Cx35.5 and GluR2 was mutually exclusive (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis of immunolabeling data shown in the figure.

claim: Cx35.5 labeling covered the majority of the club ending contact area.
source: Yet, while Cx35.5 labeling covered the majority of the area, labeling for GluR2 was substantially lower and limited to the contact's peripheral margin (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunolabeling and expansion microscopy shown in figures.

claim: GluR2 labeling was substantially lower than Cx35.5 and limited to the contact's peripheral margin.
source: Yet, while Cx35.5 labeling covered the majority of the area, labeling for GluR2 was substantially lower and limited to the contact's peripheral margin (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from immunolabeling and expansion microscopy shown in figures.

claim: GluR2 is constrained to the periphery of club ending contacts.
source: Estimates of the relative intensity of Cx35.5 vs. GluR2 in each ROI showed that, while GluR2 is constrained to the periphery, Cx35.5 is homogeneously distributed through the contact area (Figure 2E and F; see figure legend and 'Materials and methods' section for statistical analysis).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of fluorescence distribution shown in figures.

claim: Cx35.5 is homogeneously distributed through the club ending contact area.
source: Estimates of the relative intensity of Cx35.5 vs. GluR2 in each ROI showed that, while GluR2 is constrained to the periphery, Cx35.5 is homogeneously distributed through the contact area (Figure 2E and F; see figure legend and 'Materials and methods' section for statistical analysis).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of fluorescence distribution shown in figures.

claim: The distribution of GluR2 and Cx35.5 at club endings is consistent with previous EM reconstruction of club endings in adult goldfish, at which specializations for transmitter release were found to be restricted to the periphery of the contact.
source: This distribution is consistent with previous EM reconstruction of CEs in adult goldfish (Tuttle et al., 1986), at which specializations for transmitter release were found to be restricted to the periphery of the contact.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with previous EM studies supported by citation.

claim: While gap junctions occupy most of the club ending surface, chemical transmission occupies a smaller and peripheral portion.
source: Thus, while GJs occupy most of the surface, chemical transmission occupies a smaller and peripheral portion, suggesting that most of the contact operates as an electrical synapse.
evidence: This is inferred from the spatial distribution of gap junction proteins versus glutamate receptors.

claim: Labeling for Cx35.5 in expansion samples was characterized by well-defined puncta distributed throughout the contact area.
source: Rather than diffusely distributed, labeling for Cx35.5 in expansion samples was characterized by well-defined puncta distributed throughout the contact area, suggesting that they each might represent an individual GJ plaque.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on expansion microscopy data.

claim: Each Cx35.5-positive punctum might represent an individual gap junction plaque.
source: Rather than diffusely distributed, labeling for Cx35.5 in expansion samples was characterized by well-defined puncta distributed throughout the contact area, suggesting that they each might represent an individual GJ plaque.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed punctate labeling pattern.

claim: Double labeling for Cx35.5 and Cx34.1 showed a high degree of colocalization at club ending contact areas.
source: Consistent with this interpretation, double labeling for Cx35.5 and Cx34.1 (Figure 3A and C) showed a high degree of colocalization at CE contact areas (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis of immunolabeling data shown in figures.

claim: A high degree of colocalization was found between labeling for Cx35.5 and ZO1.
source: A high degree of colocalization (Figure 3B and D, Figure 3—video 1) was also found between labeling for Cx35.5 and ZO1 (Figure 3F; see figure legend for statistical analysis).
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis of immunolabeling data shown in figures.

claim: Labeling for Cx35.5 and Cx34.1 colocalized at single puncta.
source: Moreover, labeling for Cx35.5 and Cx34.1 colocalized at single puncta, as indicated by line scan of individual puncta.
evidence: This is supported by line scan analysis of immunolabeling data.

claim: Line scan of samples labeled for Cx35.5 and Cx34.1 indicated the presence of labeling for these proteins at single punctum.
source: Line scan of samples labeled for Cx35.5 and Cx34.1 indicated the presence of labeling for these proteins at single punctum (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by line scan analysis shown in the figure.

claim: The peak of maximum intensity for the pre-and postsynaptic connexins was aligned.
source: Strikingly, while the peak of maximum intensity for the pre-and postsynaptic connexins was aligned (Figure 4C), the peak of maximum intensity for Cx35.5 always preceded that of ZO1 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by line scan analysis shown in the figure.

claim: The peak of maximum intensity for Cx35.5 always preceded that of ZO1.
source: Strikingly, while the peak of maximum intensity for the pre-and postsynaptic connexins was aligned (Figure 4C), the peak of maximum intensity for Cx35.5 always preceded that of ZO1 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by line scan analysis shown in the figure.

claim: The spatial offset between Cx35.5 and ZO1 is consistent with ZO1b being postsynaptically localized.
source: This is consistent with the fact that, while Cx35.5 is presynaptically localized, ZO1b, one of the two zebrafish orthologs of ZO1, was reported to be postsynaptic.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed spatial offset and prior knowledge about ZO1b localization.

claim: The observed distance between the peaks of fluorescence for Cx35.5 and ZO1 was not due to differences in the wavelength of the fluorophores due to uncompensated chromatic aberration.
source: The observed distance between the peaks of fluorescence was not due to the differences in the wavelength of the fluorophores due to uncompensated chromatic aberration as it remained when secondary antibodies were swapped (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is supported by control experiments with swapped secondary antibodies shown in figures.

claim: The finding confirms previous conclusions that ZO1b is only located at postsynaptic hemiplaques.
source: The finding confirms previous conclusions reached with biochemical and chimera analysis indicating that ZO1b is only located at postsynaptic hemiplaques (Lasseigne et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by the current experimental data and previous research cited.

claim: Expansion increases resolution by increasing the distance between pre- and postsynaptic sites.
source: By increasing the distance between pre- and postsynaptic sites, expansion increases resolution, making it possible to explore differences in the composition of GJ hemiplaques.
evidence: This is an inference based on the principles of expansion microscopy.

claim: Each puncta correlates to a gap junction.
source: Thus, altogether, our findings indicate that each puncta correlates to a GJ.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the colocalization and line scan data.

claim: Puncta labeled for Cx35.5 showed a high degree of variability in number and size.
source: Puncta labeled for Cx35.5 (Figure 5A and B), which we established each represent a GJ, showed a high degree of variability in number and size (see inset of Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of expansion microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: The number of gap junctions per club ending averaged 36.73 ± 1.287.
source: Overall, the number of GJs per CE averaged 36.73 ± 1.287 (n = 11 CEs from four fish), and their area ranged from 0.06 to 1.99 µm2.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of expansion microscopy data.

claim: The area of gap junctions at club endings ranged from 0.06 to 1.99 µm2.
source: Overall, the number of GJs per CE averaged 36.73 ± 1.287 (n = 11 CEs from four fish), and their area ranged from 0.06 to 1.99 µm2.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of expansion microscopy data.

claim: After correcting for the expansion factor, the areas of the gap junctions were estimated to be between 4 and 148 nm2.
source: After correcting for the expansion factor (13×), the areas of the GJs were estimated to be between 4 and 148 nm2.
evidence: This is calculated from the measured areas after accounting for the expansion factor.

claim: Gap junctions at club endings contain 49–1775 connexons, assuming connexons in gap junction plaques are organized in a crystalline fashion with a density of 12,000 connexons/µm2.
source: Assuming that connexons in GJ plaques are organized in a crystalline fashion with a density of 12,000 connexons/µm2 (Kamasawa et al., 2006), we estimated that GJs at CEs contain 49–1775 connexons, and the total junctional area represents an average of 12,425 ± 493.76 connexons per CE.
evidence: This is calculated based on the measured gap junction areas and an assumption about connexon density supported by citation.

claim: The total junctional area represents an average of 12,425 ± 493.76 connexons per club ending.
source: Assuming that connexons in GJ plaques are organized in a crystalline fashion with a density of 12,000 connexons/µm2 (Kamasawa et al., 2006), we estimated that GJs at CEs contain 49–1775 connexons, and the total junctional area represents an average of 12,425 ± 493.76 connexons per CE.
evidence: This is calculated based on the measured gap junction areas and an assumption about connexon density.

claim: Electrical transmission at zebrafish club endings is mediated by multiple gap junctions containing a variable number of channels.
source: Thus, electrical transmission at zebrafish CEs is mediated by multiple GJs containing a variable number of channels.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the quantitative analysis of gap junction number and size.

claim: Previous electron microscopy analysis exposed the presence of adherens junctions in close proximity to neuronal gap junctions, including those at club endings in goldfish and larval zebrafish.
source: Previous electron microscopy analysis exposed the presence of AJs in close proximity to neuronal GJs, including those at CEs in goldfish and larval zebrafish (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by reference to an electron micrograph.

claim: Adherens junctions are known to initiate and mediate the maturation and maintenance of cell–cell contacts, including gap junctions.
source: AJs are known to initiate and mediate the maturation and maintenance of cell–cell contacts, including GJs, at which a wealth of evidence suggests a close functional interaction (Shaw et al., 2007; Defourny and Thiry, 2021; Thomas et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: A wealth of evidence suggests a close functional interaction between adherens junctions and gap junctions.
source: AJs are known to initiate and mediate the maturation and maintenance of cell–cell contacts, including GJs, at which a wealth of evidence suggests a close functional interaction (Shaw et al., 2007; Defourny and Thiry, 2021; Thomas et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Recent immunohistochemical analysis revealed the association between components of adherens junctions and Cx36 in various mammalian structures.
source: Recent immunohistochemical analysis revealed the association between components of AJs and Cx36 in various mammalian structures (Nagy and Lynn, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to recent research.

claim: Expansion for Cx35.5, N-cadherin, and ß-catenin showed that labeling for adherens junction components seems equally distributed through the synaptic contact.
source: Expansion for Cx35.5, transmembrane protein N-cadherin, and the intracellular protein ß-catenin, the latter two being major structural components of AJs, showed that labeling for AJs components seems equally distributed through the synaptic contact (Figure 6B–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from expansion microscopy and immunolabeling shown in figures.

claim: Labeling for N-cadherin and ß-catenin was diffuse, less structured, and did not colocalize with Cx35.5.
source: In contrast to Cx35.5, which is characterized by well-defined puncta reminiscent of GJs, labeling for N-cadherin and ß-catenin was diffuse, less structured, and did not colocalize with Cx35.5 (Figure 6B; see figure legend for statistical analysis).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from expansion microscopy and colocalization analysis shown in figures.

claim: The labeling for N-cadherin was interleaved with Cx35.5 puncta.
source: Rather, the labeling for N-cadherin (Figure 6C) and ß-catenin (Figure 6E) was interleaved with Cx35.5 puncta, as illustrated by line scan analysis in the margins of CE contacts (Figure 6D and F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from expansion microscopy and line scan analysis shown in figures.

claim: The labeling for ß-catenin was interleaved with Cx35.5 puncta.
source: Rather, the labeling for N-cadherin (Figure 6C) and ß-catenin (Figure 6E) was interleaved with Cx35.5 puncta, as illustrated by line scan analysis in the margins of CE contacts (Figure 6D and F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from expansion microscopy and line scan analysis shown in figures.

claim: In 'en face' views, labeling for N-cadherin was broadly distributed throughout the surface of the contact, appearing to engulf Cx35.5-labeled puncta.
source: Furthermore, in 'en face' views, labeling for N-cadherin (Figure 6G) and ß-catenin (Figure 6H) was broadly distributed throughout the surface of the contact, appearing to engulf Cx35.5-labeled puncta.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from expansion microscopy shown in figures.

claim: In 'en face' views, labeling for ß-catenin was broadly distributed throughout the surface of the contact, appearing to engulf Cx35.5-labeled puncta.
source: Furthermore, in 'en face' views, labeling for N-cadherin (Figure 6G) and ß-catenin (Figure 6H) was broadly distributed throughout the surface of the contact, appearing to engulf Cx35.5-labeled puncta.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from expansion microscopy shown in figures.

claim: Some degree of colocalization between N-cadherin/ß-catenin and Cx35.5 was observed, likely due to fluorophore amplification of the close spatial association between gap junctions and adherens junctions.
source: While labeling for N-cadherin and ß-catenin was interleaved with Cx35.5 labeling, we observed some degree of colocalization (Figure 6B) likely due to fluorophore amplification of the close spatial association between GJs and AJs (see Figure 6A).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed colocalization and the known close spatial association.

claim: Labeling for Cx35.5 and the gap junction scaffold ZO1 was equally proportional at club ending contact areas.
source: As expected, labeling for Cx35.5 and the GJ scaffold ZO1 was equally proportional (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of fluorescence shown in the figure.

claim: Similar proportionality was found for fluorescence of N-cadherin and Cx35.5, and ß-catenin and Cx35.5.
source: Similar proportionality was found for fluorescence of N-cadherin and Cx35.5, and ß-catenin and Cx35.5 (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of fluorescence shown in the figure.

claim: Fluorescence of GluR2 represented a smaller fraction than that of Cx35.5 labeling.
source: In contrast, fluorescence of GluR2 represented a smaller fraction than that of Cx35.5 labeling (Figure 7C; see figure legend for statistical analysis).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of fluorescence shown in the figure.

claim: Less than 19% of the club ending contact area was occupied by GluR2.
source: Less than 19% was occupied by GluR2, while around 73% of the contact was occupied by similar amounts of Cx35.5 and AJs.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of area occupancy.

claim: Around 73% of the club ending contact was occupied by similar amounts of Cx35.5 and adherens junctions.
source: Less than 19% was occupied by GluR2, while around 73% of the contact was occupied by similar amounts of Cx35.5 and AJs.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of area occupancy.

claim: About 8% of the club ending contact area was not labeled for Cx35.5, adherens junction proteins, or GluR2.
source: About 8% of the contact area was not labeled for these antibodies, either corresponding to the surface membrane between the structures recognized by labeling or to the presence of additional synaptic components.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of area occupancy.

claim: The unlabeled area at club endings either corresponds to the surface membrane between the structures recognized by labeling or to the presence of additional synaptic components.
source: About 8% of the contact area was not labeled for these antibodies, either corresponding to the surface membrane between the structures recognized by labeling or to the presence of additional synaptic components.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about the nature of the unlabeled area.

claim: While chemical synapses are restricted to a small and peripheral area of the club ending contact, most of the contact surface is occupied by multiple gap junctions of variable size which are interleaved and closely associated to adherens junctions.
source: Thus, while chemical synapses are restricted to a small and peripheral area of the contact, most of the contact surface is occupied by multiple GJs of variable size which are interleaved and closely associated to AJs (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental data presented.

claim: The structural complexity of chemical synapses has long been recognized.
source: The structural complexity of chemical synapses has long been recognized.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Structural complexity is a hallmark of immunological synapses.
source: Structural complexity is also a hallmark of immunological synapses (Dustin, 2014), specialized functional contacts which quickly assemble between a thymus-derived lymphocyte and an antigen-presenting cell (Dustin, 2012; Dustin and Groves, 2012).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Both chemical and immunological synapses share a general molecular organization combining cell adhesion molecules, usually restricted to the periphery of the contacts, with those more centrally located and responsible for providing intercellular communication.
source: Both chemical and immunological synapses share a general molecular organization combining cell adhesion molecules, usually restricted to the periphery of the contacts, with those more centrally located and responsible for providing intercellular communication (Dustin and Colman, 2002).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The structural arrangement of club ending electrical synapses might apply to the general organization of chemical and immunological synapses.
source: Our results indicate that this structural arrangement might also apply to the CE electrical synapse.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed structural organization at club endings.

claim: The finding that adherens junctions surround gap junctions all through the club ending contact is consistent with the general organization of chemical and immunological synapses.
source: That is, our finding that AJs surround GJs all through the contact is consistent with the general organization of chemical and immunological synapses, at which adhesion molecules are located in the periphery of the communicating mechanism.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with the known organization of other synapse types.

claim: Electrical synapses combine cell adhesion molecules with those responsible for mediating intercellular communication, similar to chemical and immunological synapses.
source: Thus, just as chemical and immunological synapses, electrical synapses also seem to combine cell adhesion molecules with those responsible for mediating intercellular communication.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the observed structural organization.

claim: Adherens junctions could be considered components of electrical synapses based on similarities in overall organization across synapses and evidence of functional interactions with gap junctions.
source: Based on these similarities in the overall organization across synapses and evidence of functional interactions with GJs (see above), we propose that AJs could be considered components of electrical synapses.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the observed structural organization and functional evidence.

claim: The distribution of adhesion molecules at electrical synapses might serve to define their synaptic boundary.
source: While additional components are likely to contribute to electrical transmission, the distribution of adhesion molecules at electrical synapses might serve to define their synaptic boundary, an arrangement that might be used as a template to identify electrical synapses in other structures.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal about the functional role of adherens junctions.

claim: The arrangement of adhesion molecules at electrical synapses might be used as a template to identify electrical synapses in other structures.
source: While additional components are likely to contribute to electrical transmission, the distribution of adhesion molecules at electrical synapses might serve to define their synaptic boundary, an arrangement that might be used as a template to identify electrical synapses in other structures.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal about potential applications of the findings.

claim: A close association between components of adherens junctions and Cx36 was observed at various mammalian brain structures.
source: Supporting this notion, a close association between components of AJs and Cx36 was observed at various mammalian brain structures (Nagy and Lynn, 2018) and was suggested they share a common molecular complex (Nagy and Lynn, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to research in mammalian systems.

claim: It was suggested that adherens junction components and Cx36 share a common molecular complex.
source: Supporting this notion, a close association between components of AJs and Cx36 was observed at various mammalian brain structures (Nagy and Lynn, 2018) and was suggested they share a common molecular complex (Nagy and Lynn, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to research in mammalian systems.

claim: Multiple Cx36-labeled puncta engulfed by N-cadherin labeling were observed at cell–cell contacts between the somata of neurons of the mesencephalic nucleus of the trigeminus in mice.
source: As in CEs, multiple Cx36-labeled puncta engulfed by N-cadherin labeling were also observed at cell–cell contacts between the somata of neurons of the mesencephalic nucleus of the trigeminus in mice (see Figure 8 in Nagy and Lynn, 2018), indicating that this arrangement is not a unique feature of fish mixed synapses but might also apply to electrical synapses elsewhere.
evidence: This is supported by citation to observations in mammalian systems.

claim: The arrangement of multiple gap junctions engulfed by adherens junction components is not a unique feature of fish mixed synapses but might also apply to electrical synapses elsewhere.
source: As in CEs, multiple Cx36-labeled puncta engulfed by N-cadherin labeling were also observed at cell–cell contacts between the somata of neurons of the mesencephalic nucleus of the trigeminus in mice (see Figure 8 in Nagy and Lynn, 2018), indicating that this arrangement is not a unique feature of fish mixed synapses but might also apply to electrical synapses elsewhere.
evidence: This is an inference based on observations in both fish and mammalian systems.

claim: Expansion microscopy of club endings offered the possibility of identifying the structures that support electrical transmission and the components that together form an electrical synapse.
source: In summary, as single synaptic contact, expansion microscopy of CEs offered the possibility of identifying the structures that support electrical transmission and, therefore, the components that together form an electrical synapse, which can be used to define electrical synapses throughout animal connectomes.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the significance of the findings.

claim: The components identified at club endings can be used to define electrical synapses throughout animal connectomes.
source: In summary, as single synaptic contact, expansion microscopy of CEs offered the possibility of identifying the structures that support electrical transmission and, therefore, the components that together form an electrical synapse, which can be used to define electrical synapses throughout animal connectomes.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications of the findings.

claim: Defining the components of an electrical synapse will help expose their functional diversity as different synapses might operate with different numbers of gap junctions and synaptic arrangements.
source: Moreover, defining the components of an electrical synapse will help expose their functional diversity as different synapses might operate with different numbers of GJs and synaptic arrangements.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the implications of the findings.

claim: All experiments were performed in 5 dpf zebrafish, Danio rerio.
source: All experiments were performed in 5 dpf zebrafish, Danio rerio.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the experimental model.

claim: Experiments were carried out in the Tol-056 enhancer trap line.
source: Experiments were carried out in the Tol-056 enhancer trap line (Satou et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the experimental model supported by citation.

claim: The lateral and axial resolutions of the microscope system were estimated to range between 248.9 to 322 nm and 429.44 to 557.04 nm, respectively, depending on the excitation wavelength used.
source: We estimated the lateral and axial resolutions of our microscope (Wilhelm et al., 2010) to range between 248.9 to 322 nm and 429.44 to 557.04 nm, respectively, depending on the excitation wavelength used (488, 543, 633).
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the imaging system.

claim: After correcting for the linear expansion factor (3.9×), the lateral and axial resolutions after expansion are expected to range between 63.81 to 82.77 nm and 110.11 to 142.83 nm, respectively.
source: After correcting for the linear expansion factor (3.9×), the lateral and axial resolutions after expansion are expected to range between 63.81 to 82.77 nm and 110.11 to 142.83 nm, respectively.
evidence: This is calculated from the microscope resolution and the expansion factor.

claim: Gap junctions are ubiquitous structures present in virtually every tissue of the organism.
source: While GJs are ubiquitous and present in virtually every tissue of the organism providing metabolic coupling (Goodenough and Paul, 2009), they additionally serve as a pathway of low resistance for the spread of electrical currents between neurons (and cells of the heart), the main form of signaling in the brain, which is fast enough to operate within the time frame required for decision-making by neural circuits (Bennett, 1997; Alcamí and Pereda, 2019).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Expansion microscopy is complementary to electron microscopy.
source: Expansion microscopy is complementary to a different representation of reality, electron microscopy, which is capable of providing fine details of the structures, but can inform, to a lesser degree, their biochemical composition.
evidence: This is an inference about the relationship between different microscopy techniques.

claim: Electron microscopy is capable of providing fine details of structures but can inform, to a lesser degree, their biochemical composition.
source: Expansion microscopy is complementary to a different representation of reality, electron microscopy, which is capable of providing fine details of the structures, but can inform, to a lesser degree, their biochemical composition.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of the capabilities and limitations of electron microscopy.

claim: Expansion microscopy was more easily capable of exposing the complete contact area of the terminal compared to electron microscopy.
source: Unlike the more labor-intensive electron microscopy, expansion microscopy was more easily capable of exposing the complete contact area of the terminal, while additionally revealing its biochemical composition (i.e., because of its bias toward exposing intramembrane particles, freeze fracture EM of CEs did not reveal additional synaptic components between GJs; Yao et al., 2014; Tuttle et al., 1986; Kohno and Noguchi, 1986; Pereda et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of the two techniques and supported by citations.

claim: Freeze fracture electron microscopy of club endings did not reveal additional synaptic components between gap junctions because of its bias toward exposing intramembrane particles.
source: Unlike the more labor-intensive electron microscopy, expansion microscopy was more easily capable of exposing the complete contact area of the terminal, while additionally revealing its biochemical composition (i.e., because of its bias toward exposing intramembrane particles, freeze fracture EM of CEs did not reveal additional synaptic components between GJs; Yao et al., 2014; Tuttle et al., 1986; Kohno and Noguchi, 1986; Pereda et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of freeze fracture EM supported by citations.

claim: Expansion microscopy unambiguously exposed the postsynaptic location of ZO1b.
source: Confirming this conclusion, our expansion microscopy unambiguously exposed the postsynaptic location of ZO1b.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from expansion microscopy and line scan analysis.

claim: Both ZO1b and ZO1a might be restricted to postsynaptic hemiplaques, although with different functions.
source: Moreover, because the antibody recognizes both ZO1b and ZO1a, our data indicates that, although with different functions, both ZO1 orthologs might be restricted to postsynaptic hemiplaques.
evidence: This is an inference based on the antibody specificity and the observed localization.

claim: Adherens junctions are dynamic cell–cell adhesion complexes that are continuously assembled and disassembled.
source: AJs are dynamic cell–cell adhesion complexes that are continuously assembled and disassembled.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about adherens junctions.

claim: Adherens junctions are formed by a complex of proteins that include cadherins and catenins (ß and α).
source: They are formed by a complex of proteins that include cadherins and catenins (ß and α).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about adherens junction composition.

claim: Growing evidence indicates a functional relationship between adherens junctions and gap junctions.
source: Growing evidence indicates a functional relationship between AJs and GJs (Shaw et al., 2007; Meyer et al., 1992; Li et al., 2005; Wei et al., 2005; Dalva et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to research on the relationship between these structures.

claim: It was generally accepted that gap junctions form via lateral diffusion of hemichannels following microtubule-mediated delivery to the plasma membrane.
source: While it was generally accepted that GJs form via lateral diffusion of hemichannels following microtubule-mediated delivery to the plasma membrane, more recent evidence obtained in cell expression systems shows that microtubules actually tether to the AJ, facilitating delivery of vesicles containing connexin hemichannels directly to the cell–cell border of the GJ (Shaw et al., 2007).
evidence: This represents a previous understanding in the field.

claim: More recent evidence shows that microtubules tether to the adherens junction, facilitating delivery of vesicles containing connexin hemichannels directly to the cell–cell border of the gap junction.
source: While it was generally accepted that GJs form via lateral diffusion of hemichannels following microtubule-mediated delivery to the plasma membrane, more recent evidence obtained in cell expression systems shows that microtubules actually tether to the AJ, facilitating delivery of vesicles containing connexin hemichannels directly to the cell–cell border of the GJ (Shaw et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to recent research.

claim: The process of gap junction channel delivery depends on the interaction of microtubules with plus-end-tracking protein (+TIP) EB1, its interacting protein p150 (Glued), and the adherens junction proteins N-cadherin and ß-catenin.
source: This process depends on the interaction of microtubules with plus-end-tracking protein (+TIP) EB1, its interacting protein p150 (Glued), and the AJ proteins N-cadherin and ß-catenin (Shaw et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to research on the molecular mechanisms.

claim: The process of gap junction channel delivery requires homophilic interactions between N-cadherins.
source: Furthermore, the evidence indicates that this process also requires homophilic interactions between N-cadherins.
evidence: This is supported by citation to research on the molecular mechanisms.

claim: Similar peripheral delivery of gap junction channels to adherens junctions was observed in sensory epithelial cells of the cochlea.
source: Similar peripheral delivery of GJ channels to AJs was observed in sensory epithelial cells of the cochlea (Defourny and Thiry, 2021), indicating that this mechanism also operates in tissues.
evidence: This is supported by citation to research in tissue systems.

claim: The mechanism of gap junction channel delivery to adherens junctions operates in tissues.
source: Similar peripheral delivery of GJ channels to AJs was observed in sensory epithelial cells of the cochlea (Defourny and Thiry, 2021), indicating that this mechanism also operates in tissues.
evidence: This is an inference based on observations in tissue systems supported by citation.

claim: Adherens junction formation hierarchically regulates the formation of gap junctions in cardiac pacemaker cells.
source: Also consistent with a close functional relationship between these structures, AJ formation hierarchically regulates the formation of GJs in cardiac pacemaker cells (Thomas et al., 2021), adjusting the excitability and coupling of these neurons in the context of their pacemaking function.
evidence: This is supported by citation to research in cardiac cells.

claim: Adherens junction formation adjusts the excitability and coupling of cardiac pacemaker cells in the context of their pacemaking function.
source: Also consistent with a close functional relationship between these structures, AJ formation hierarchically regulates the formation of GJs in cardiac pacemaker cells (Thomas et al., 2021), adjusting the excitability and coupling of these neurons in the context of their pacemaking function.
evidence: This is supported by citation to research in cardiac cells.

claim: Electrical transmission at each zebrafish club ending terminal is mediated on average by about 35 gap junctions.
source: However, electrical transmission at each zebrafish CE terminal is mediated on average by about 35 GJs, suggesting that they together operate as a functional unit.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of expansion microscopy data.

claim: Multiple gap junctions at club endings together operate as a functional unit.
source: However, electrical transmission at each zebrafish CE terminal is mediated on average by about 35 GJs, suggesting that they together operate as a functional unit.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of multiple gap junctions.

claim: Chemical synapses operate with dramatically different numbers of release sites, ranging from a single one at synaptic terminals of PHP cells on the M-cell to up to 700 in the Calyx of Held.
source: Like chemical synapses that operate with dramatically different numbers of releases sites, ranging from a single one at synaptic terminals of PHP cells on the M-cell (Korn et al., 1982; Korn et al., 1981) to up to 700 in the Calyx of Held (Sätzler et al., 2002; Taschenberger et al., 2002), electrical synapses could function with different number of GJs.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Electrical synapses could function with different numbers of gap junctions.
source: Like chemical synapses that operate with dramatically different numbers of releases sites, ranging from a single one at synaptic terminals of PHP cells on the M-cell (Korn et al., 1982; Korn et al., 1981) to up to 700 in the Calyx of Held (Sätzler et al., 2002; Taschenberger et al., 2002), electrical synapses could function with different number of GJs.
evidence: This is an inference based on analogy with chemical synapses.

claim: Operating with multiple gap junctions might result in more reliable electrical transmission as only a very small fraction of channels are known to be functional at individual gap junctions.
source: Operating with multiple GJs might result in more reliable electrical transmission as only a very small fraction of channels are known to be functional at individual GJs (Flores et al., 2012; Curti et al., 2012; Szoboszlay et al., 2016; Marandykina et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an inference based on knowledge about gap junction channel function supported by citations.

claim: Only a very small fraction of channels are known to be functional at individual gap junctions.
source: Operating with multiple GJs might result in more reliable electrical transmission as only a very small fraction of channels are known to be functional at individual GJs (Flores et al., 2012; Curti et al., 2012; Szoboszlay et al., 2016; Marandykina et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Because of the wide variation in size, gap junctions at club endings might coexist at different states of conductance.
source: Because of the wide variation in size, GJs at CEs might coexist at different states of conductance (Bukauskas et al., 2000).
